rationale: Selected memories temporarily inhibit their own reselection and recover by fixed decay. This creates feedback from prior internal selection into future competition without generating prose, inventing facts, adding context tokens, or depending on learned prediction estimates.
interpretation: Refractory selection advances only if it reduces consecutive top-K memory-set overlap by at least 0.10 absolute while retaining at least 90% of both immediate retrieval score and discounted future retrieval-rank utility on BOTH frozen evidence blocks. Future utility uses a four-tick horizon with 0.8 per-tick discount. A zero-penalty ablation must collapse exactly to ordinary retrieval. Passing permits a later prospective replication test, not live or shadow activation.
